title: Brain2Qwerty and where this project starts
subtitle: Diagrams for the Fidetype wiki. Edit the .drawio files, then run: node tools/drawio/build.js

slides.title: 1. What Brain2Qwerty does
slides.caption: Meta's model reads brain signals while a person types. Then it predicts the typed text. The signal comes from finger movement, not from thought.

slides.title: 2. Version 1 and version 2
slides.caption: v1 needs the time of each key press. v2 does not. v2 uses 10 times more data per person and an LLM to write the sentence.

slides.title: 3. The five layers of a BCI
slides.caption: Layers 2 to 5 are software. Layer 1 needs a lab and money. Start at layers 3 and 4: data and decoding.

slides.title: 4. Long-term project options
slides.caption: Four options. A, B and D can start now on your computer. C needs more compute.

slides.title: 5. Proposed roadmap
slides.caption: Start with learning. Then build an open toolkit. Then do research on a small real-time decoder.

slides.title: 6. Architecture: six layers
slides.caption: Six layers turn neural data into reliable text. The trust core is the heart of the project. Green parts are open source; red dashed parts stay private later.

slides.title: 7. Data flow
slides.caption: Data goes from a source through a decoder into the NeuralTextStream format. The trust core then picks an action: commit, offer choices, ask, or abstain.

slides.title: 8. Roadmap (trust-layer direction)
slides.caption: Set up first. Then write two papers: calibrated text, then causal decoding. Then release the benchmark and connect real devices.

slides.title: 9. Milestones (1-week target)
slides.caption: The user set the targets on 2026-11-08. M0 ends on 11-09. M1 and M2 run in parallel, then M3 and M4, then M5, then the code parts of M6 and M7. All end by 11-15. The dashed lane holds items that depend on outside people. They have no dates.

slides.title: 10. Open-source path
slides.caption: Six stages take Fidetype from a paper to a neutral standard, then to a company. Each stage borrows from SGLang, LangChain, OpenTelemetry or BIDS. Success means decoders that emit NeuralTextStream, not stars.

slides.title: 11. Long-term roadmap: from v0.1 to a full standard
slides.caption: After v0.1, thirteen phases run in four lanes. We build the spec, SDKs, collector, adapters, trust layer, benchmark and demo. Yellow phases P12 (intent beyond text) and P13 (benchmark hub) come last and do not change priorities. Grey dashed items depend on outside people. Replay comes before hardware, and the demo and benchmark come before outreach.

slides.title: 12. Streaming trust layer (M4-03)
slides.caption: The layer reads NeuralTextStream events one at a time and keeps a state per session. At the end of each utterance it runs the frozen trust core and emits one final decision with provenance. A partial result gives only a preview. User feedback moves the online threshold, but never below the frozen commit_p.
